# A test reads the prop of a node that shows a context, on every target: what
# the test set, or the default, and inside a provider the component writes,
# the provider's. Read through the test's own instance the context answers
# nothing but the test, which the read was refused as though it could not
# name; left standing, html read `.value` off nothing and the Go targets
# called an accessor nobody wrote.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout '2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout '2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout '2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout '2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout '2 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=android --language=kotlin app.sngl
stdout '2 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

context[string] #greeting("hello")

component page ui.node {
    ui.text #shown(value=greeting)
    greeting("inner") {
        ui.text #inner(value=greeting)
    }
}

// A node showing a context is read like any other.
func testANodeShowsAContext(t test.Test, c page) {
    t.assert(c.shown.value == "hello")
}

func testASetContextShows(t test.Test, c page) {
    t.setContext(greeting, "hi")
    t.assert(c.shown.value == "hi")
    t.assert(c.inner.value == "inner")
}

ui.window {
    page()
}
